전도서-4-1.title: 전도서 4장 1절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-1.exegesis: 22. (Compare Ec 3:12 ; 5:18 ). Inculcating a thankful enjoyment of God's gifts, and a cheerful discharge of man's duties, founded on fear of God; not as the sensualist ( Ec 11:9 ); not as the anxious money-seeker ( Ec 2:23 ; 5:10-17 ). his portion-- in the present life. If it were made his main portion, it would be "vanity" ( Ec 2:1 ; Lu 16:25 ). for who, &c.-- Our ignorance as to the future, which is God's "time" ( Ec 3:11 ), should lead us to use the present time in the best sense and leave the future to His infinite wisdom ( Mt 6:20 , 25, 31-34 ).

전도서-4-2.title: 전도서 4장 2절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 4 Ec 4:1-16 . 1. returned-- namely, to the thought set forth ( Ec 3:16 ; Job 35:9 ). power-- Maurer, not so well, "violence." no comforter-- twice said to express continued suffering without any to give comfort ( Is 53:7 ).

전도서-4-3.title: 전도서 4장 3절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-3.exegesis: 2. A profane sentiment if severed from its connection; but just in its bearing on Solomon's scope. If religion were not taken into account ( Ec 3:17 , 19 ), to die as soon as possible would be desirable, so as not to suffer or witness "oppressions"; and still more so, not to be born at all ( Ec 7:1 ). Job ( Job 3:12 ; 21:7 ), David ( Psa 73:3 , &c.), Jeremiah ( Jr 12:1 ), Habakkuk ( Ha 1:13 ), all passed through the same perplexity, until they went into the sanctuary, and looked beyond the present to the "judgment" ( Psa 73:17 ; Ha 2:20 ; 3:17 , 18 ). Then they saw the need of delay, before completely punishing the wicked, to give space for repentance, or else for accumulation of wrath ( Ro 2:15 ); and before completely rewarding the godly, to give room for faith and perseverance in tribulation ( Psa 92:7-12 ). Earnests, however, are often even now given, by partial judgments of the future, to assure us, in spite of difficulties, that God governs the earth.

전도서-4-5.title: 전도서 4장 5절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-5.exegesis: 4. right-- rather, "prosperous" (see on Ec 2:21 ). Prosperity, which men so much covet, is the very source of provoking oppression ( Ec 4:1 ) and "envy," so far is it from constituting the chief good.

전도서-4-6.title: 전도서 4장 6절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-6.exegesis: 5. Still the fool (the wicked oppressor) is not to be envied even in this life, who "folds his hands together" in idleness ( Pr 6:10 ; 24:33 ), living on the means he wrongfully wrests from others; for such a one eateth his own flesh-- that is, is a self-tormentor, never satisfied, his spirit preying on itself ( Is 9:20 ; 49:26 ).

전도서-4-7.title: 전도서 4장 7절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-7.exegesis: 6. Hebrew; "One open hand (palm) full of quietness, than both closed hands full of travail." "Quietness" (mental tranquillity flowing from honest labor), opposed to "eating one's own flesh" ( Ec 4:5 ), also opposed to anxious labor to gain ( Ec 4:8 ; Pr 15:16 , 17 ; 16:8 ).

전도서-4-9.title: 전도서 4장 9절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-9.exegesis: 8. not a second-- no partner. child-- "son or brother," put for any heir ( De 25:5-10 ). eye-- ( Ec 1:8 ). The miser would not be able to give an account of his infatuation.
전도서-4-9.theologicalNote: 8. not a second-- no partner. child-- "son or brother," put for any heir ( De 25:5-10 ). eye-- ( Ec 1:8 ). The miser would not be able to give an account of his infatuation.

전도서-4-10.title: 전도서 4장 10절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-10.exegesis: 9. Two-- opposed to "one" ( Ec 4:8 ). Ties of union, marriage, friendship, religious communion, are better than the selfish solitariness of the miser ( Ge 2:18 ). reward-- Advantage accrues from their efforts being conjoined. The Talmud says, "A man without a companion is like a left hand without the right.

전도서-4-11.title: 전도서 4장 11절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-11.exegesis: 10. if they fall-- if the one or other fall, as may happen to both, namely, into any distress of body, mind, or soul.
전도서-4-11.theologicalNote: 10. if they fall-- if the one or other fall, as may happen to both, namely, into any distress of body, mind, or soul.

전도서-4-12.title: 전도서 4장 12절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-12.exegesis: 11. (See on 1Ki 1:1 ). The image is taken from man and wife, but applies universally to the warm sympathy derived from social ties. So Christian ties ( Lu 24:32 ; Ac 28:15 ).
전도서-4-12.theologicalNote: 11. (See on 1Ki 1:1 ). The image is taken from man and wife, but applies universally to the warm sympathy derived from social ties. So Christian ties ( Lu 24:32 ; Ac 28:15 ).

전도서-4-13.title: 전도서 4장 13절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-13.exegesis: 12. one-- enemy. threefold cord-- proverbial for a combination of many--for example, husband, wife, and children ( Pr 11:14 ); so Christians ( Lu 10:1 ; Col 2:2 , 19). Untwist the cord, and the separate threads are easily "broken."
전도서-4-13.theologicalNote: 12. one-- enemy. threefold cord-- proverbial for a combination of many--for example, husband, wife, and children ( Pr 11:14 ); so Christians ( Lu 10:1 ; Col 2:2 , 19). Untwist the cord, and the separate threads are easily "broken."

전도서-4-14.title: 전도서 4장 14절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-14.exegesis: 13. The "threefold cord" [Ec 4:12] of social ties suggests the subject of civil government. In this case too, he concludes that kingly power confers no lasting happiness. The "wise" child, though a supposed case of Solomon, answers, in the event foreseen by the Holy Ghost, to Jeroboam, then a poor but valiant youth, once a "servant" of Solomon, and ( 1Ki 11:26-40 ) appointed by God through the prophet Ahijah to be heir of the kingdom of the ten tribes about to be rent from Rehoboam. The "old and foolish king" answers to Solomon himself, who had lost his wisdom, when, in defiance of two warnings of God ( 1Ki 3:14 ; 9:2-9 ), he forsook God. will no more be admonished-- knows not yet how to take warning (see Margin) God had by Ahijah already intimated the judgment coming on Solomon ( 1Ki 11:11-13 ).

전도서-4-15.title: 전도서 4장 15절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-15.exegesis: 14. out of prison-- Solomon uses this phrase of a supposed case; for example, Joseph raised from a dungeon to be lord of Egypt. His words are at the same time so framed by the Holy Ghost that they answer virtually to Jeroboam, who fled to escape a "prison" and death from Solomon, to Shishak of Egypt ( 1Ki 11:40 ). This unconscious presaging of his own doom, and that of Rehoboam, constitutes the irony. David's elevation from poverty and exile, under Saul (which may have been before Solomon's mind), had so far their counterpart in that of Jeroboam. whereas ... becometh poor-- rather, "though he (the youth) was born poor in his kingdom" (in the land where afterwards he was to reign).

전도서-4-16.title: 전도서 4장 16절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-4-16.exegesis: 15. "I considered all the living," the present generation, in relation to ("with") the "second youth" (the "legitimate successor" of the "old king," as opposed to the "poor youth," the one first spoken of, about to be raised from poverty to a throne), that is, Rehoboam. in his stead-- the old king's.
